questions.prompt: The standard metal for a can never fails. A cheaper metal fails 5% of the time, and each failure costs $40 to replace. By how much must the cheaper metal's price per can be below the standard price for its expected cost per can to be strictly lower?
questions.prompt_markup: The standard metal for a can never fails. A cheaper metal fails 5% of the time, and each failure costs $40 to replace. By how much must the cheaper metal's price per can be below the standard price for its expected cost per can to be strictly lower?

questions.grading_note: Form required: "more than $2.00"; exactly $2.00 cheaper gives equal expected costs.
